text: The rate limit of Kestrel-6 is 4450 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Unlike Avocet-5, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Lark-7 is $4685k. Nobody should assume the budget of Lark-7 applies to Avocet-5, the budget differs.
Unlike Teal-3, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Kestrel-6 is the Quito datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Kestrel-6 applies to Teal-3, the datacenter differs.
Avocet-5 runs in the Osaka datacenter, next to its database. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Questions about Teal-3 start with its owner, the Ember team; they triage anything filed against it. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Avocet-5 is implemented in Go; the language was chosen for its tooling.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Avocet-5, which is 850 requests per minute.

Unlike Teal-3, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Kestrel-6 is Soren Valdivia. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Kestrel-6 applies to Teal-3, the pager rotation differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The pager rotation for Avocet-5 is run by Mateo Abernathy; alerts page them first.
For Lark-7 the port is 4271. Changing the port needs a change ticket. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Lark-7 reaches its retirement date on January 20, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.

The service Bittern-5 takes traffic on port 2312, and the port is fixed across every environment.

Unlike Kestrel-6, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Teal-3 is Nadia Okonkwo. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Teal-3 applies to Kestrel-6, the pager rotation differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
